Shade from real geometry.

Buildings from OpenStreetMap and trees measured by airborne LiDAR cast shadows for the sun at the time you choose.

02

The sun moves while you walk.

Shade is recomputed every 15 minutes along the way, and each street uses the sidewalk on its shadier (or sunnier) side.

HOW THIS MAP WORKS

,

A working geometry and routing model, not a validated heat-navigation service.

Study area

Buildings and streets

Building footprints and walkable ways come from OpenStreetMap (official OSM API). Heights use the OSM height tag, then floor count × 3.3 m, then an assumed 12 m (about 39 ft) where neither exists. Streets and buildings are included up to 150 m beyond the dashed boundary so walks near the edge still route correctly.

Tree canopy (LiDAR)

Sun and shade

SunCalc gives the sun position for the chosen date and time. Every building and crown is swept away from the sun by its height divided by the tangent of solar elevation (capped at 400 m). Each street segment is sampled every 10 m to find the share in shade. Trees count in summer only; winter assumes leaf-off. The time is held constant for the whole walk.

How routes are compared

Dijkstra's algorithm finds the shortest walk. Seven penalty weights on sun (summer) or shade (winter) produce alternatives. An alternative section replaces the matching part of the shortest walk only if it improves exposure and adds no more than the extra time you allow. This is a heuristic, not a guaranteed optimum.

Known gaps

Street centerlines stand in for sidewalks. Terrain, awnings, building relations in OSM, canopy change since the surveys, live closures, indoor routes and accessibility are not modeled.
